solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beast with personality is going with the upwardly mobile classes

parts.note: a cat is a beast, here a domestic animal
ego is the self, one's personality

parts.words: is going with the upwardly mobile
parts.note: something moving upward rises, so 'is going ... upwardly' gives rises

explanation.surface: A social commentator sneers at a creature of strong character mixing with the social climbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile classes' reads as a phrase about social climbers, but 'classes' is the verb definition and the rest gives the verb meaning goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify things is to sort them into categories, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Income changes over time — not much money here though

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word income are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's income fluctuates over the years, though there is never much to speak of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' tells you the anagram of INCOME sits around the T. 'here though' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimo is a tiny coin, a hundredth of a peseta or other unit, so it is very little money.

clue.text: Model turns up hugging brown giants

indicators.note: hugging says one piece is wrapped round another
in a down clue, turns up says the piece reads from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to sit for an artist is to model
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A fashion model turns up embracing a suntanned pair of hulking men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' is a verb here, to pose for a painter, not a noun; 'turns up' reverses it in this down clue, and 'hugging' wraps it round the brown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth, so the word now means giants.

clue.text: Exceptionally large car to carry Democrat who lived in White House?

indicators.note: to carry says the pieces hold another letter between them
exceptionally suggests the letters of large are arranged out of the ordinary

parts.note: taken as written
a Ford is a make of car
D is the usual abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: A huge automobile is laid on to ferry a Democratic politician to the presidential residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Democrat' looks like part of the definition, but Ford was a Republican; 'to carry' puts the Democrat letter between the anagram ('Exceptionally') and the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerald Ford was US president in 1974-77, so he lived in the White House.

clue.text: Food from recipe with something from freezer?

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on a doctor's prescription
ice is what comes out of a freezer

explanation.surface: A cook makes a dish from a recipe with something frozen added.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe (Latin recipe, 'take') is the prescription symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is a staple grain eaten as a foodstuff all over the world.

clue.text: Request from one wanting to be frisked? I've no explanation!

definitions.text: Request from one wanting to be frisked?
definitions.meaning: someone keen to be patted down would invite a search of their person
a colloquial reply meaning I have no idea

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the everyday shrug literally, as an invitation to be searched.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'I don't know', and literally asks to be searched.

clue.text: Chemical that could be abused — therefore litres must have outlet

parts.note: so means therefore
a vent is an outlet for air or gas

explanation.surface: A warning that a misused chemical needs ventilation when measured out by the litre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must have' is just a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvents such as glue are inhaled in solvent abuse, so they are chemicals open to misuse.

clue.text: Caretaker has rubbish taken back after start of year

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the date

parts.note: the first day of the year is 1 January, written Jan I

indicators.note: taken back says the word for rubbish is read backwards

parts.note: rot means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A school caretaker carries the bins out again just after New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of year' is not one letter but the date of New Year's Day written with a Roman numeral; 'taken back' turns the rubbish round and 'after' places it behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor looks after a building, the same job as a caretaker.

clue.text: Dumping one boy in the course of travelling by air!

indicators.note: in the course of says the pieces go inside the travelling word

parts.note: jetting means flying by jet
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Sarcastic remark about leaving a child behind while flying off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the course of' puts the Roman numeral and the boy inside the flying verb; the exclamation mark points to the joke of ditching a child mid-flight.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison cargo is to throw it overboard, so jettisoning means dumping.

clue.text: Fellow permitted to make flower arrangement

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A man is given leave to do the floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a garland or wreath of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: Business operation in which branches will be reduced

definitions.text: Business operation in which branches will be reduced

parts.words: Business operation in which branches will be reduced
parts.note: reads like a company closing outlets, but the branches are those of a tree and the operation is cutting them back

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests corporate downsizing; the branches are on trees and the 'operation' is surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree surgeons prune and cut back the limbs of trees as a trade.

clue.text: Altering peculiar shape

indicators.note: peculiar says the letters of the first word are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a figure is changing strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a three-sided geometric shape.

clue.text: Son to take science (not Phys.!) and English — that's the plan

parts.note: chem is the short name for chemistry, a science that is not physics

explanation.surface: A family decides their boy will study chemistry rather than physics, plus English.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not Phys.!)' steers you from PHYS to the other common school science abbreviation, CHEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan of action.

clue.text: Police primarily lenient, about rogue's minor offence

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Police primarily lenient, about rogue's minor offence' has no anagram indicator: wordplay is an anagram of POLICE + L around CAD, and the blog supplies 'sloppy' which the clue lacks.
annotationWithheld.clue: Police primarily lenient, about rogue's minor offence

clue.text: Element in domestic appliance

definitions.meaning: a household device for pressing clothes

explanation.definitionFit: Iron is both a metallic element and the appliance for smoothing laundry.

clue.text: Bad effects maybe following a school period?

parts.note: after means following
maths is a lesson, a period in a school timetable

explanation.surface: Perhaps unpleasant consequences come after a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is a link; MATHS, the British word for math, is the lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Aftermaths are the consequences of a disaster, usually unpleasant ones.

clue.text: Go down when caged by judicial decision

indicators.note: caged by says one piece is enclosed within another

parts.note: a decree is an order from a court
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A criminal is sent down, locked up by order of the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down' reads as being sent to prison, but it is simply the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrease is to become less, that is to go down.

clue.text: Be so strict about care of new mum etc.

indicators.note: about says the letters of the preceding words are moved around

explanation.surface: A midwife is told to be firm in handling a mother after childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics is the medical field dealing with pregnancy, childbirth and mothers after birth.

clue.text: Sentimental folk in dirty homes, including old female

indicators.note: including says the pieces are put inside the homes

parts.note: sties are pigsties, filthy places to live

explanation.surface: Tender-hearted people live in squalor and take in an elderly woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Softies are soft-hearted, easily moved people.

clue.text: One may have gone to pot

definitions.text: One may have gone to pot

parts.words: One may have gone to pot
parts.note: going to pot means deteriorating, but here it means turning to cannabis

explanation.walkthrough: Pot is cannabis; someone who takes drugs is one who has turned to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user is someone who takes substances like cannabis.

clue.text: Just the sort of agitator to create a storm in a teacup?

definitions.text: Just the sort of agitator to create a storm in a teacup?

parts.words: Just the sort of agitator to create a storm in a teacup?
parts.note: an agitator causing fuss over nothing, and also a teaspoon swirling the tea in a cup

explanation.walkthrough: A storm in a teacup is a fuss about little; literally a spoon swirling the tea makes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrer is a troublemaker, and also an implement that agitates a drink.

clue.text: Skin's burning up — pain in Nice

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: red describes something burning hot
mal is French for pain, as spoken in Nice

explanation.surface: Someone suffering sunburn complains of the pain on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermal means relating to the skin, as skin's does.

clue.text: Company with home front that's weak

indicators.note: front says the home piece goes before the company

parts.note: in means at home
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A business working from a home base is a feeble outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak, especially through age or illness.

clue.text: The bloke's in a den — it's tacky

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar or den
he's is 'he is', the bloke being he

explanation.surface: A man is in a seedy joint, and it is all rather tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tacky' looks like 'cheap and vulgar', matching the den, but it means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adhesive is sticky, which is what tacky means of glue or paint.

clue.text: When there's no holiday in winter months

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: Pupils grumble that there are no holidays during the winter months.
explanation.definitionFit: A school term is the period of teaching between holidays.

clue.text: There's elegance about this writer's

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'There's elegance about this writer's' has no definition: wordplay is GRACE around I'M, and nothing names a facial expression.

clue.text: Fish-like creature to hit hunted victim

parts.note: to lam is to beat or hit
prey is an animal that is hunted

explanation.surface: A predator strikes the animal it has been chasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamprey is an eel-like jawless vertebrate, not a true fish.

clue.text: Restore mall that's broken up — using this finally?

definitions.text: Restore mall that's broken up — using this finally?

indicators.note: broken up says the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Repairing a damaged shopping centre's paving, finishing with heavy machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a road roller would flatten new surfacing at the end of the repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamroller flattens new asphalt, the last stage of resurfacing.
